title: RAW residue from one organ, suitable for another: recipient restriction preserves the material description
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Full Galen III.9 joins faculty necessity to recipient-relative appropriateness. A shared description-restriction constructor preserves one material witness and its origin while adding a recipient argument; it does not turn classification into a transformation or an actual feeding event. No target words or forms selected.

design.mechanism: Apply one recipient-relative predicate to an existing material description by conjunction on the SAME bound material variable. The result retains the original description, including source/origin, rather than replacing it with a new material kind or a destination label.
design.unit: The entire single HTML paragraph p277 comprising Galen On the Natural Faculties III.9, through the dogs/faeces and liver-residue comparisons; next paragraph begins III.10. The older faculty-only excerpt is not called the complete paragraph.
design.contrast: One relational description with origin and recipient roles versus recipient-specific material names whose origin is supplied elsewhere; also a temporal transformation account that introduces a product rather than qualifying the existing description.
design.prediction: Qualifying the same liver-residue description for spleen, gall-bladder and kidneys keeps its origin fixed while varying the recipient. It does not identify the witnesses across the three qualifications, erase their origin, or predict an actual transfer. A whole written account must express any additional token identity or event.

source.whole_content: Spleen and other nourished parts attract appropriate material and reject foreign material, with powers of retention and alteration; all four faculties are necessary. Human faeces please dogs; liver residues are appropriate to different named organs. The comparison is part of this paragraph, not a separate source unit.
qualifications: Pleasingness in the dog comparison is not silently strengthened to actual nourishment or a therapeutic benefit.
Some residues suit spleen, others gall-bladder or kidneys. No universal suitability, exhaustive partition, mutually exclusive suitability sets or fixed identity of physical portions is stated here.
The paragraph appeals to prior demonstration. This backward reference is retained; the proof is not recreated from the paragraph alone.
Historical claims, not medical advice. Suitability, faculty possession, actual attraction, retention, alteration and successful nourishment remain different assertions.

formal_contract.status: Explicit hypothetical content construction, not a complete source parser or target grammar.
formal_contract.MaterialDescription: A predicate on material witnesses in an explicitly stated context. A witness may stand for a source-described kind/member under quantified discourse; it is not automatically an observed physical portion.
formal_contract.RESIDUE_FROM: SourceRole x Context -> MaterialDescription; RESIDUE_FROM(a,c)(x) means that x has the stated residual-origin relation to a in c.
formal_contract.PROPER_FOR: MaterialWitness x RecipientRole x Context -> Proposition; suitability in the historical nutritional frame. It is not an event or a synonym of residue, palatability, benefit or successful assimilation.
formal_contract.law: FOR_RECIPIENT(b,c)(D) = lambda x: D(x) AND PROPER_FOR(x,b,c). D and PROPER_FOR share the same x; the predicate's recipient argument b does not overwrite D's source argument a.
formal_contract.projection_law: Any written witness of FOR_RECIPIENT(b,c)(RESIDUE_FROM(a,c)) still satisfies RESIDUE_FROM(a,c) and is proper for b. No new material witness, source reassignment, motion or transformation is generated by the constructor.
formal_contract.application_limit: The source description must have a compatible context. A context mismatch cannot be repaired by an implicit time, patient or frame cast. No automatic anaphora or single unique material token is assumed.
formal_contract.open_world: An unasserted suitability relation is unknown. The three named recipient qualifications need not be disjoint or exhaustive. Residue-from(a) alone does not imply foreign-to(a), unsuitable-for(a), or unsuitable-for-every-recipient.
formal_contract.no_temporal_inference: Conjoining origin and suitability does not describe an executed journey from a to b or a before/after role change. A temporal account may coexist, but must supply its own event and lineage assertions.
formal_contract.polysemy_limit: One constructor has one relational denotation at every use. Varying its explicit recipient is argument substitution, not a new lexical sense. Conversely, a word with distinct senses cannot be reclassified as this constructor merely because the resulting English sentences sound plausible.

witness_and_quantifier_policy.source_preserving_minimum: Retain a nonempty appropriate-residue description for each named recipient in the source's general account. Do not instantiate a physical sample, clinical case, quantity or exhaustive residual stock.
witness_and_quantifier_policy.same_within_one_claim: If a later reading explicitly introduces witness x under one qualification, both its origin and its suitability concern that same x. This is a logical shared argument, not independent evidence of material-token conservation.
witness_and_quantifier_policy.across_claims: Witnesses xS/xG/xK are not automatically identical or different. The source's some/others contrast remains visible, but stronger disjoint-class or token-inequality claims require separately declared interpretation and written ownership.
witness_and_quantifier_policy.unknown_cells: No cross-recipient exclusion table is supplied. The construction cannot acquire a unique solution by treating all other origin/suitability combinations as false. No source-derived finite quantity or three-object inventory.

full_paragraph_obligations: Spleen and extension to liver, veins, arteries, heart and other nourished parts; every generalized participant needs scope.
Appropriate versus foreign as recipient-relative descriptions, with attraction/rejection assertions preserved in their general rather than invented episode reading.
Retention/alteration powers over what is attracted, without silently asserting that every possible item has actually been attracted or assimilated.
Four faculties required for nutrition, no converse guarantee of actual successful nutrition; prior-demonstration and handmaid language retained as discourse content.

Dog/faeces comparison with pleasingness and human origin intact, plus the distinct organ-suitability relation. One generic PROPER_FOR cannot absorb both predicates without an additional declared bridge.
All three organ qualifications and their shared residual-origin description. No one-word macro for the complete paragraph or for all named organs.

serious_rivals.contract: The text names different material kinds appropriate to different recipients, and expresses their liver origin elsewhere. Such names may denote classes and recur across many portions.
serious_rivals.difference: The proposed constructor would preserve source ownership inside the qualified description; the rival may state it through a separate relation. Both can reproduce the source. The distinction must be located in the written composition, not inferred from the presence of different recipients.

serious_rivals.contract: The expression records a destination or intended recipient, while a different clause asserts nutritional suitability.
serious_rivals.difference: Designation alone does not entail PROPER_FOR. A complete source-faithful reading could still state suitability elsewhere; no target rejection follows from the present source graph alone.

serious_rivals.contract: A residue undergoes a process and its product is suitable for a recipient. Such change can coexist with origin provenance.
serious_rivals.difference: This account adds an event/product or changed-state assertion that description restriction alone does not entail. It is not refuted simply because the source paragraph lacks that assertion. A fixed target reading would need to write the event and bind its material arguments.

smallest_consequence_and_falsifier.positive_opportunity: One unchanged qualification construction can take the same origin-bearing description with different recipient arguments. A later explicit reference to the qualified witness must preserve its source role while keeping the recipient distinct.
smallest_consequence_and_falsifier.failure_of_fixed_descendant: Reject a fixed descendant if its repeated constructor silently replaces the origin with the recipient, introduces a new product without written process content, requires a physical same-token identification across generic cases, converts unknown suitability to false, or omits a full-paragraph obligation.
smallest_consequence_and_falsifier.decision_change: Two whole written cases retaining both arguments under one construction would constrain a compound reading more than separate residue/food names. A third recipient case must use the same law without a new alias or special frame. A mere semantic table of proper recipients does not justify an executor.
smallest_consequence_and_falsifier.not_ready: No written realization or target case exists here. Exploratory authoring is permitted without confirmed meanings; the missing complete writer still prevents calling this a manuscript test or a finished reading.
